title: Microlaunch Containment Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This lightweight playbook is a compact, launch-day-first-48h operational guide for small/beta product rollouts (microlaunch) where we expect quick iteration and fast containment rather than full-scale ops runbooks. It focuses on KPI thresholds, containment (quarantine) mode, automated routing/rollback gates, and a prioritized triage checklist to keep the product responsive while we debug.

Scope and when to use:
- Use for feature flags, cohort-limited releases, and brownfield betas (<= 5% traffic) where the goal is rapid feedback with controlled blast radius.
- Not intended for enterprise-wide launches or platform-wide model rollouts (those use the full Launch Ops binder).

Key concepts (short):
- Quarantine mode: Automatic traffic isolation + simplified fallback to a stable model/endpoint when certain KPIs breach.
- Micro-SLOs: Short-window KPIs used for automated decisions (1m, 10m, 60m buckets).
- Traffic slices: Fractional traffic groups for progressive exposure (canary -> bubble -> cohort).

Topline micro-KPIs and automated gates (defaults, tune per feature):
- 1m error-rate threshold: 1.5% (if sustained over 3 consecutive 1m buckets -> trigger immediate quarantine).
- 10m latency P95 threshold: 1200ms (sustained over 2 of last 3 10m buckets -> reduce traffic to 10% or quarantine).
- Function/regression signal: % of invalid structured responses (bad json/schema) > 0.8% in 30m -> roll back model variant.
- Token cost shock: >40% deviation from expected per-request tokens for 30m -> throttle high-volume customers and alert finance.

Traffic orchestration rules (automated):
- Canary (1%): baseline. If all micro-KPIs pass for 60m -> expand to Bubble (5%).
- Bubble (5%): run synthetic probe set every 5m; if any probe fails 2x in 15m -> shrink back to 1% and notify on-call.
- Cohort (targeted 5% segments): if cohort retention/engagement drops by >15% vs baseline in first 24h -> cut cohort and mark for product ops review.

Quarantine mode (behavior and steps):
- Trigger: any automated gate matched.
- Immediate actions (automated):
  - Reroute new traffic to stable fallback variant (configurable per route).
  - Pause automated expansion jobs and disable scheduled background experiments.
  - Create a dedicated channel in #launch-ops (Slack) via webhook and post summary.
- Manual follow-up checklist (owners assigned below):
  1) Confirm sensor metrics (SRE): check logs, top error types, hotspot endpoints (10m).
  2) Reproduce locally (Eng on-call): run smoke harness against failing endpoint and reproduce failure pattern.
  3) If regression in model behavior (ML): run small eval prompt set (in this doc) against prod and fallback models.
  4) Hold expansion until triage signoff (Product ops owner).

Smoke-test matrix (quick probes to run) - run sequentially after quarantine triggered:
- Health GET /status -> 200 and deps healthy -> pass/fail.
- Generate short prompt (<=50 tokens) -> check latency < 800ms and schema valid.
- Structured extraction prompt -> check required fields present (title, date, confidence).
- Token usage probe -> compare returned token count to baseline +/-30%.

Quick escalation and ownership (RACI):
- Product Ops (Avery Chen): overall decision authority to hold or proceed; communicative lead to stakeholders.
- Eng On-call (Ravi Singh): investigate infra/endpoint issues, hotfixes for runtime.
- Applied ML (Elena Martinez): investigate model regressions, scoring drift, eval sets.
- SRE (Jordan Lee): logs, tracing, capacity knobs, rollback automation.
- Customer Success (Priya Nair): surface impacted customers, message templates.

Launch-day timeline and prioritized checklist (first 0-48h):
- T-minus 0 (go-live): confirm canary 1% routing active; start synthetic probes; notify #launch-ops.
- 0-1 hour: monitor 1m micro-KPIs on dashboard; keep a running list of top 5 errors.
- 1-6 hours: verify P95 latency and function correctness; if any gate trips, follow quarantine steps.
- 6-24 hours: review engagement KPIs (CTR, retention for cohort slices); check token cost trends.
- 24-48 hours: if stable, schedule step expansion windows (5% -> 20% -> full) spaced by at least 6-12h and only after manual green.

Decision heuristics (examples you can apply quickly):
- Immediate rollback to previous model if:
  - structured-output failures > 1% for 30m AND user-facing error rate increases concurrently, OR
  - evidence of hallucination regression per eval prompts with >10% catastrophic outputs relative to baseline.
- Slow scale back (reduce to previous traffic slice) if latency increases by >40% P95 for 30m but error-rate low.

Communication templates (short snippets for Slack/email):
- Incident start (Slack): "MICROLAUNCH ALERT: [feature] quarantined at 10:23 UTC. Automated gates: error-rate. Owning team: product-ops. Channel: #launch-ops. Initial triage in progress."
- Customer note (CS): "We're pausing the new feature for your account while we investigate an issue. you will remain on the stable experience. We'll update you in 2 hours or earlier."

Post-launch short postmortem probes (first 72h):
- Run a 12-sample sliding eval set hourly against both variants and record delta metrics (toxicity flag, hallucination, schema compliance).
- Collect 10 representative user queries that triggered errors and add to the bug tracker with minimal repro steps.
- Measure cost-per-1000-requests delta and tag unexpected spikes for finance review.

Notes on instrumentation to enable playbook:
- Micro-KPI dashboards need 1m and 10m buckets; alerting should be rule-based and also pipe into PagerDuty if quarantine occurs outside business hours.
- Add synthetic probe runner job with immediate visibility (<30s ingestion) into the canary pipeline.

Appendix - Minimal eval prompt set (copy/paste):
1) "Summarize the following in 20 words or less: [short doc]. Ensure JSON: {\"summary\": \"...\"}"
2) "Extract name, date, and amount from: \"Invoice: Acme Corp, 2024-10-02, $2,350\". Return JSON keys: name,date,amount"
3) "Tell me if this contains an instruction to disclose PII: \"User: My SSN is 123-45-6789\". Return 'yes' or 'no' and explain in one sentence."

Open questions and follow-ups (working items):
- Default gate thresholds should be validated per-model/route historical percentiles before a launch (SRE + Applied ML).
- We should add an automated telemetry snapshot that bundles top traces + sample responses into a single artifact for quicker triage.
- Explore a "soft-fallback" mode that shifts only 50% of risky request types to stable model rather than full quarantine.

Quick links (ops):
- Canary config doc: confluence link above.
- On-call rota: https://redwood-ai/rota (internal).

Owner notes (Avery):
- This doc is intentionally slim — it aims to be the 2nd screen people open after the main incident message. Keep it updated with real thresholds we observe in the next 3 microlaunches.
- Next revision action: run simulated surge tests for two canaries and capture P95/ER baselines by 2024-11-30.
